title: The History of The Witcher | Books, Games and Netflix | Gaming History
description: The full history of The Witcher: Andrzej Sapkowski's books, the CD Projekt Red games, Witcher 3's awards and sales, the Netflix series, the new Witcher 3 remaster and what comes next.

sections.heading: A monster hunter with white hair
sections.script: A man with white hair, two swords and a very bad feeling about this. Geralt of Rivia has become one of the most famous heroes in all of fantasy, and his story started long before any video game. The Witcher began as a short story in Poland, grew into a series of books, and then became a game franchise that has sold more than ninety million copies. In this video we follow the whole journey: Andrzej Sapkowski's books, the first game from a small Polish studio called CD Projekt Red, the huge success of The Witcher Three, the Netflix series, and the exciting news from this year, including a remaster that arrived just a few weeks ago. Grab your silver sword and let's begin.

sections.heading: It started with a short story
sections.script: The Witcher began in nineteen eighty six, when the Polish author Andrzej Sapkowski entered a short story called The Witcher into a contest held by the magazine Fantastyka. It won third place, and it was the start of his career as a writer. Readers wanted more, so Sapkowski wrote a number of further stories about the monster hunter Geralt, which were collected into books. In nineteen ninety four he began the main series, The Witcher Saga, with the novel Blood of Elves. He wrote roughly one book a year until the fifth and final part of the saga came out in nineteen ninety nine. Later he returned to the world with the prequel novel Season of Storms in twenty thirteen, and with Crossroads of Ravens in twenty twenty four.

sections.heading: The first game in two thousand seven
sections.script: The first video game, simply called The Witcher, came out for computers in two thousand seven. It was made by CD Projekt Red, a studio from Poland. The game used a modified version of an engine from BioWare, the famous role playing studio, and it let players make choices that changed how the story went. It was not perfect, but it showed ambition and a real love for the books. An enhanced edition followed in two thousand eight with extra content and improvements. For a young studio it was a brave start, and it laid the foundation for everything that came later.

sections.heading: Assassins of Kings
sections.script: In twenty eleven came The Witcher Two: Assassins of Kings. This time the studio built its own engine, called REDengine, and the difference was easy to see. The game looked far better, told a darker political story, and offered branching paths that gave the choices even more weight. It first launched on PC, and the Xbox three sixty version arrived in April of twenty twelve together with an Enhanced Edition, which was a free upgrade for existing owners and added hours of new content. The Witcher Two helped CD Projekt Red earn a reputation among role playing fans as a studio that listens to players and keeps improving its games long after launch.

sections.heading: Wild Hunt changes everything
sections.script: On May nineteenth, twenty fifteen, The Witcher Three: Wild Hunt launched for PC, PlayStation four and Xbox One. It put Geralt in a huge open world, with a search for his adopted daughter Ciri at the center, and it filled that world with side quests that felt like small stories of their own. Players and critics were amazed by how much care went into even the smallest task. The game became the studio's biggest success by far and made CD Projekt Red a household name. Its mix of dark fantasy, strong writing and freedom set a new standard for open world role playing games, and many other studios still point to it as an inspiration today.

sections.heading: Awards and two big expansions
sections.script: The praise came quickly. At The Game Awards in December of twenty fifteen, The Witcher Three won Game of the Year, and CD Projekt Red was also named Developer of the Year. The studio then did something rare: it supported the game with large paid expansions that felt like full games. Hearts of Stone arrived on October thirteenth, twenty fifteen, with a tale of a mysterious man and a cursed bargain. Blood and Wine followed on May thirty first, twenty sixteen, taking Geralt to the sunny land of Toussaint. Many fans still say Blood and Wine is one of the best expansions ever made, and it gave the story a warm and fitting farewell.

sections.heading: Selling like never before
sections.script: The numbers tell their own story. In its report for the first quarter of twenty twenty six, CD Projekt said that The Witcher Three has passed sixty five million copies sold. The whole Witcher game series has now sold more than ninety million copies, according to the same company update. That is remarkable for a game that launched more than ten years ago, and it shows how steadily new players keep discovering Geralt, helped by sales, new platforms and the Netflix series. For a franchise that began with a small studio and a single Polish book series, reaching ninety million copies is a milestone few games ever reach.

sections.heading: Geralt on Netflix
sections.script: The books and games also led to a television series. Netflix released the first season of The Witcher at the end of twenty nineteen, with Henry Cavill playing Geralt of Rivia. He starred in the first three seasons, and the third season was released in two parts in June and July of twenty twenty three. After that, Liam Hemsworth took over the role, and season four arrived on Netflix on October thirtieth, twenty twenty five. The series brought many new viewers to the world of the Continent, and plenty of them went on to try the books and the games for the first time. It is a nice example of one story finding fans across many different kinds of entertainment.

sections.heading: The remaster is here
sections.script: Now to the newest chapter. The Witcher Three: Wild Hunt Remastered launched on September twenty ninth, twenty twenty six, for PC, PlayStation five and Xbox Series X and S, and it also arrived as a native version on the Nintendo Switch Two. It includes both earlier expansions, and it is free for people who already own the game. Early reviews have been very positive, and one outlet gave the Switch Two version a perfect score. CD Projekt Red has also announced a third expansion called Songs of the Past, made together with the studio Fool's Theory, and it is planned for twenty twenty seven. So after more than ten years, there is brand new Witcher Three content on the way.

sections.heading: What comes next
sections.script: And what about the future? At The Game Awards in December of twenty twenty four, CD Projekt Red revealed The Witcher Four with a cinematic trailer, and it confirmed that Ciri, now grown up, is the playable hero of a new saga. The game is built on Unreal Engine five. The company has not announced a release date, and it has said the game will not launch before twenty twenty seven. A remake of the very first Witcher game is also in the works at Fool's Theory, supervised by CD Projekt Red, which was announced back in October of twenty twenty two. There is a lot to look forward to for fans of the series.

sections.heading: Which Witcher story is your favorite
sections.script: From a short story in nineteen eighty six to a franchise with more than ninety million games sold, The Witcher shows what happens when a great world meets creators who care. Now we want to hear from you. Which game is your favorite, The Witcher, The Witcher Two or the legendary Wild Hunt? Do you prefer the books, the games or the Netflix series? And who do you want to play as in The Witcher Four? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history, like the video and subscribe for more gaming history, and may your swords stay sharp. Toss a coin to your Witcher, and see you in the next video.
